exercise.name: Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees

reference.title: Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching). The band, usually across the front of the hips, is drawn as two strands from the rack uprights behind to the hands, which hold it at the sides of the hips.

equipment: Resistance band (two strands, or a long band round the hips)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you drive the hips forward, inhale as they go back.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s forward, short squeeze, about 2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: pick a band you can drive through to full tall kneeling for every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a stronger band; longer squeeze

cues.text: Kneel on a mat facing away from a rack, knees hip width, toes tucked. Hold the band strands at the sides of your hips so the band pulls them back; sit the hips back toward the heels with a long back.
Breathe out, squeeze the glutes and drive the hips forward until you are tall on the knees.
Tall kneeling: hips fully forward, ribs down, glutes squeezed; do not lean back.
Breathe in and let the band draw the hips back toward the heels, hinging with a long back.
Brief pause with the hips back, then drive again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back and arching the low back at the top
mistakes.fix: Finish tall with the ribs down; the hips move, the low back stays still.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back when sitting back
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips with a long back.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band yank the hips back
mistakes.fix: Control the lowering over about 2 s.
Keep the knees hip width and planted on the mat.

kinematics.norm: From hips back (about 60-90 degrees of flexion) to neutral at the top (clinical opinion)
The thighs swing from well behind vertical (hips toward the heels) to vertical at the top (clinical opinion)
Leaning forward with the hinge at the bottom, upright at the top (clinical opinion)
Elastic tension rises as the hips move forward, so the load is highest at the top, where the glutes are shortest (clinical opinion)
About 1 s forward, a short squeeze, about 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Resistance Band Hip Thrusts on Knees, video (movement reference)
Krause Neto, Soares, Vieira et al. 2020, gluteus maximus activation during common strength and hypertrophy exercises: a systematic review (J Sports Sci Med 19(1):195-203)
Macadam and Feser 2019, gluteus maximus EMG excitation during dynamic body-weight hip extension: a systematic review (Int J Sports Phys Ther 14(1):14-31; PMC6350668)

cautions: Stop if pain in the low back, hips or knees, numbness or tingling occurs.
Kneel on a mat or pad.
Anchor the band low and securely round the uprights and check it for nicks; a snapping band can whip back.
Band tension is user-chosen: start light.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: add padding or do a glute bridge instead.
Low-back discomfort: shorten the range and keep the trunk more upright.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Prime mover: drives the hips forward to full extension against the band; the band load is highest at the top.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension with the knee bent.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: The large adductor assists hip extension from the flexed position.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the long back in the hinge; they should not arch the low back at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Steady the knees on the mat.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Prime mover: drives the hips forward to full extension against the band; the band load is highest at the top.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension with the knee bent.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: The large adductor assists hip extension from the flexed position.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the long back in the hinge; they should not arch the low back at the top (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Steady the knees on the mat.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down so the hips, not the low back, finish the move (Macadam 2019 reviewed bracing and glute activity).
